problem: Abandoned public catalogue reads continued SDK work after the client disconnected; fallback queries could follow the abandoned read.

baseline.expected: Disconnected response aborts the SDK transport
baseline.method: Actual Express router, async context, service and installed SDK, with loopback client and mocked origin fetch

implementation: Opt in public catalogue handlers to a request-local cancellation signal, cleaning listeners after finish or close.
Combine parent disconnect cancellation with existing artwork and translation deadlines; bind SDK builders rather than singleton clients.
Stop later pages, strategies and fast-set fallbacks after cancellation; avoid writes to a closed response.
Keep normal HTTP/cache/identity behaviour and authenticated pricing/admin operations outside the opt-in scope.

limitations: Offline origin transport is mocked; real Express loopback, route/context/service and installed Supabase SDK are exercised.
503 cancellation can re-enter the SDK fetch callback with an already aborted signal, but native-fetch-compatible transport sends no new network request.
No shared in-flight promise coalescing exists in the scoped helpers; same-route/identity concurrency verifies independent context and SDK builders.
Request disconnect cancellation is confirmed locally. Production gateway disconnect propagation, database resource recovery, and installed-device retrieval are unverified.
This P2 repair is not evidence of the cause or cure of the separate production database connection/statement failures.
